Hi Alice / Nimbus team —

Thanks for committing time yesterday. Per our call, I’m kicking off a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for your Dedicated deployment and the evaluation plan for capacity sizing. The goal here is to align stakeholders, agree on throughput targets & test criteria, and set a realistic close timeline so Procurement can estimate costs.

Key objectives
- Confirm roles and owners from both sides
- Agree on throughput / concurrency targets for month-1 and steady-state
- Define the evaluation plan (synthetic tests, sample prompts, latency SLOs)
- Produce a procurement-ready quote and SOW by the target date below

Proposed initial targets (for discussion)
- Average sustained throughput: 300 requests/min (avg across working hours)
- Peak burst capacity: 800 requests/min for up to 10 minutes
- P95 generation latency target: <200ms (model dependent)
- Concurrent KV-backed sessions: 50 active streams

Attachments I’ve included: MAP_NimbusHealth_v1.pdf (draft MAP with milestones) and throughput_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet for you to fill in observed QPS from your test harness).

Proposed timeline
- Week 0 (this week): stakeholder confirmations + finalize test dataset
- Weeks 1–3: dedicated cluster build + evaluation window (synthetic and replay)
- Week 4: capacity tuning, final sizing recommendation
- Week 5: procurement quote / SOW delivered

Asks from your side
1) Please confirm the technical point-of-contact for orchestration & infra (we have CCed Procure + Dev Ops but would like a primary).
2) Share any guarded test prompts or regulatory constraints we should know about.
3) Procurement target date for receiving a commercial quote (Procurement asked for an internal due date; if May 10 is necessary, call it out).

Internal note: Rishi — can you own the MAP and convey commercial milestones? Marissa — would you lead sizing & runtime testing? Priyom — can you validate the latency modelling once we have sample prompts?

I’ll schedule a 30-min MAP kickoff for early next week (Mon/Tue preferred) after we get stakeholder confirmations.

Thanks,

Couple technical notes from the GPU pool perspective —

1) Baseline sizing suggestion (starting point)
- For the evaluation window, recommend a small dedicated pool: 3 x A100 80GB equivalent instances (or 4 x A10G if cost sensitivity) to run parallel synthetic loads and warm KV caches. This gives headroom to test bursts and autoscaling knobs.

2) Evaluation plan (high level)
- Synthetic replay: run a 72-hour replay of representative traffic (we’ll need a sampled dataset from Nimbus)
- Warm cache phase: 1 hour of prefix warmups to populate KV caches to simulate steady-state
- Stress burst test: 30-min 2x target burst to validate autoscaler behavior
- Latency measurement: capture p50/p95/p99 token latency and end-to-end generation time

3) Metrics & instrumentation
- We’ll instrument the Redwood Console dashboards for per-route token breakdown, model-level latency, and GPU utilization. Please ensure we have access to a sandbox telemetry endpoint or share sample logs.

4) Notes on model variants
- If Nimbus wants better throughput, we recommend testing a quantized 7B variant as a cheaper fallback for non-critical paths and a higher-capacity 13B for critical streams. We will include model-switch routing in the MAP as an optional step.

Priyom — for sizing calc, I’ll assume 24 tokens/sec on an A100 for rlhf-3b and 40 tokens/sec for a tuned 7B quantized path. If Nimbus gives us avg tokens per request, we can produce a precise GPU count.

Marissa
Eng Manager — Capacity & Deployment | Redwood Inference
